title: Create the Invoice Record
subtitle: Turn the inbound invoice into the first trusted record
scenario: It is 9:00 AM. The Invoice Inbox handed you a PDF from Northwind Fasteners. A person can read it; the workflow cannot. Extract the fields the desk needs - vendor, PO, quantity, price, total - into one structured Invoice Record every downstream step can trust.
input: INVOICE INV-58831 - Northwind Fasteners (vendor V-1042). Bill against PO-7742. 500 x M8 hex bolt, zinc @ $2.44 each. Invoice total: $1,220.00. Terms: net 30. Please remit to account on file.
instructions: Identify the invoice number and the vendor id.
Find the PO number this invoice bills against.
Capture the line quantity, the invoice unit price, and the invoice total.
Return one valid JSON object with those fields.
Use numbers (not text) for quantity, unitPrice, and invoiceTotal.
copilotPrompt: Extract structured JSON from this invoice. Return invoiceNumber, vendorId, poNumber, quantity, unitPrice, and invoiceTotal. Use numbers for quantity, unitPrice, and invoiceTotal.
successMessage: Invoice Record built. The desk now has a structured invoice every downstream step can match against.
editorHelper: Create one JSON object the workflow can reuse downstream.

intro.heading: Before you match: structure the invoice

sections.title: What this record does
sections.body: The Invoice Record turns an inbound PDF into the first structured object the payables desk can trust. Matching, duplicate checks, and payment all read this record - never the raw document.

sections.title: Why the document is not enough
sections.body: A PDF is readable by a person but opaque to software. Downstream automation needs stable fields: invoice number, vendor, PO, quantity, unit price, and total.

sections.title: Numbers must be numbers
sections.body: Quantity, unit price, and total feed arithmetic two steps later (the three-way match). Store them as numbers, not text, or the variance math cannot run.

sections.title: Who reuses it
sections.body: The Duplicate Check, the Three-Way Match, and the Payment Batch all read this record. Extracting it once and well is what lets everything after it stay automatic.

fieldGuide.meaning: The vendor's identifier for this invoice.
fieldGuide.hint: Look for the INV-##### number at the top of the document.

fieldGuide.meaning: Beacon's id for the vendor who sent the invoice.
fieldGuide.hint: The vendor id in parentheses (V-####), which ties back to the Vendor Master.

fieldGuide.meaning: The purchase order this invoice bills against.
fieldGuide.hint: The PO-#### the invoice cites - the join key for matching.

fieldGuide.meaning: The number of units billed on the line.
fieldGuide.hint: The count before the 'x' - store it as a number.

fieldGuide.meaning: The price per unit the invoice claims.
fieldGuide.lookFor: price per unit on the invoice?
fieldGuide.hint: The per-each price. Store the number only, without the dollar sign.

fieldGuide.meaning: The total amount the invoice asks Beacon to pay.
fieldGuide.lookFor: what is the invoice asking for?
fieldGuide.hint: The invoice total. Store the number only - 1220, not $1,220.00.

takeaway.heading: Invoice Record built
points: You extracted six stable fields from an unstructured PDF into one trusted record.
Amounts are stored as numbers, so the three-way match can compute the price variance later.
The PO number is captured as the join key that links this invoice to its order and receipt.
The record is saved as invoice-record.json - the artifact the whole desk matches against.
The workflow can now match, de-duplicate, and pay this invoice from structured data.
